subject: general
question:
From the given alternatives, choose the correct meaning of the idiom.

What goes around comes around.

options.text: People's actions have consequences that will eventually return to them
People's pets will eventually return home if they go out
If you throw a stone up, it will fall down
A drunkard will eventually return home

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. People's actions have consequences that will eventually return to them.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"What goes around comes around"** refers to the concept that actions, whether good or bad, have consequences that eventually return to a person. (जो करता है वही भरता है) • **Example:** If you treat others with kindness, they will eventually reciprocate because what goes around comes around. • This idiom emphasizes the moral principle of karma or the cyclical nature of actions and their outcomes. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. People's actions have consequences that will eventually return to them.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: __ • **Option 2: People's pets will eventually return home if they go out** (पालतू जानवर बाहर जाने पर अंततः घर लौट आएंगे): • This is unrelated to the idiom and reflects a literal interpretation of pets returning home. • **Example:** Cats often roam outside but eventually return home. • **Option 3: If you throw a stone up, it will fall down** (यदि आप पत्थर ऊपर फेंकते हैं, तो वह नीचे गिरेगा): • This describes a natural physical phenomenon (gravity) and does not relate to the moral or cyclical concept of the idiom. • **Example:** Stones always fall due to the force of gravity. • **Option 4: A drunkard will eventually return home** (शराबी अंततः घर लौटेगा): • This interpretation is irrelevant to the idiom's meaning and does not reflect its moral or philosophical context. • **Example:** After spending the night at the bar, the drunkard stumbled his way back home. 1ab:T189c, The correct answer is **Matanga**__.
